objects.definition: typedef unsigned char yaml_char_t;
objects.description: Alias for an unsigned byte representing a UTF-8 octet; used for YAML text buffers and strings.
Holds the %YAML version directive numbers (major, minor) for a document.
Represents a %TAG directive mapping a handle to a URI prefix.
Enumeration of stream encodings for input/output processing.
Enumeration of line break styles to use when emitting.
Enumeration describing high-level error categories produced by parser/emitter.
Marks a position in the input/output stream (index, line, column).
Enumeration of scalar presentation styles.
Enumeration of sequence presentation styles (block/flow).
Enumeration of mapping presentation styles (block/flow).

objects.definition:
typedef enum yaml_token_type_e {
    YAML_NO_TOKEN,
    YAML_STREAM_START_TOKEN,
    YAML_STREAM_END_TOKEN,
    YAML_VERSION_DIRECTIVE_TOKEN,
    YAML_TAG_DIRECTIVE_TOKEN,
    YAML_DOCUMENT_START_TOKEN,
    YAML_DOCUMENT_END_TOKEN,
    YAML_BLOCK_SEQUENCE_START_TOKEN,
    YAML_BLOCK_MAPPING_START_TOKEN,
    YAML_BLOCK_END_TOKEN,
    YAML_FLOW_SEQUENCE_START_TOKEN,
    YAML_FLOW_SEQUENCE_END_TOKEN,
    YAML_FLOW_MAPPING_START_TOKEN,
    YAML_FLOW_MAPPING_END_TOKEN,
    YAML_BLOCK_ENTRY_TOKEN,
    YAML_FLOW_ENTRY_TOKEN,
    YAML_KEY_TOKEN,
    YAML_VALUE_TOKEN,
    YAML_ALIAS_TOKEN,
    YAML_ANCHOR_TOKEN,
    YAML_TAG_TOKEN,
    YAML_SCALAR_TOKEN
} yaml_token_type_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of scanner tokens produced by yaml_parser_scan().
Represents a lexical token from the YAML scanner with variant data depending on type; memory must be freed with yaml_token_delete().

objects.definition:
typedef enum yaml_event_type_e {
    YAML_NO_EVENT,
    YAML_STREAM_START_EVENT,
    YAML_STREAM_END_EVENT,
    YAML_DOCUMENT_START_EVENT,
    YAML_DOCUMENT_END_EVENT,
    YAML_ALIAS_EVENT,
    YAML_SCALAR_EVENT,
    YAML_SEQUENCE_START_EVENT,
    YAML_SEQUENCE_END_EVENT,
    YAML_MAPPING_START_EVENT,
    YAML_MAPPING_END_EVENT
} yaml_event_type_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of high-level parsing events.
Represents a high-level parsing/emitting event with associated parameters; resources should be freed with yaml_event_delete() when applicable.
Enumeration of document node kinds.
Represents a node within a YAML document (scalar, sequence, or mapping) with style and content details.

objects.definition: typedef int yaml_node_item_t;
objects.description: Represents an index (node id) for elements within a sequence node's items stack.
Holds a key/value node id pair for mapping nodes.
In-memory representation of a YAML document, owning stacks of nodes and directives; must be deleted via yaml_document_delete().

objects.definition:
typedef int yaml_read_handler_t(void *data, unsigned char *buffer, size_t size,
        size_t *size_read);
objects.description: Application-provided callback type to supply bytes to the parser.
Internal scanner helper structure tracking potential simple key positions and requirements.

objects.description: Parser state machine enumeration used internally by the parser.
Tracks anchor name, referenced node id, and position for alias resolution during parsing.

Core parser object maintaining reader buffers, scanner state, parser state, and the current document. Initialize with yaml_parser_initialize() and destroy with yaml_parser_delete(). Set inputs and parse/scan/load via provided APIs.

objects.definition: typedef int yaml_write_handler_t(void *data, unsigned char *buffer, size_t size);
objects.description: Application-provided callback type to accept bytes from the emitter.

objects.description: Emitter state machine enumeration used internally by the emitter.

Core emitter object managing output buffers, configuration, and emission state. Initialize with yaml_emitter_initialize() and destroy with yaml_emitter_delete(). Configure outputs and encoding before emitting events/documents.

functions.name: yaml_get_version_string
functions.description: Return the libyaml version as a static NUL-terminated string in the form "X.Y.Z". Intended for runtime version checks and diagnostics. The returned pointer refers to static storage owned by the library.
requirements: Do not free or modify the returned string pointer (it points to static storage).
Thread-safety/constness of the returned pointer is unspecified; treat as read-only.

functions.name: yaml_get_version
functions.description: Retrieve libyaml’s version numbers as three integers (major, minor, patch). Values are written via the provided output pointers.
requirements: major, minor, and patch must be valid, non-NULL pointers to int.
The pointers must be writable.

functions.name: yaml_token_delete
functions.description: Free any memory owned by a token object previously produced by the parser (yaml_parser_scan). Leaves the token object in an undefined/empty state.
requirements: token must be a valid pointer to a yaml_token_t previously initialized/produced by the parser.
Do not use the token’s internal pointers after deletion.
Do not call yaml_token_delete twice on the same token object without reinitialization.

functions.name: yaml_stream_start_event_initialize
functions.description: Initialize a STREAM-START event with the specified stream encoding. Populates an empty yaml_event_t for emission or further processing.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
encoding must be one of yaml_encoding_t values; YAML_ANY_ENCODING lets the emitter choose.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_stream_end_event_initialize
functions.description: Initialize a STREAM-END event. Populates an empty yaml_event_t for emission or processing.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_document_start_event_initialize
functions.signature: int yaml_document_start_event_initialize(yaml_event_t *event, yaml_version_directive_t *version_directive, yaml_tag_directive_t *tag_directives_start, yaml_tag_directive_t *tag_directives_end, int implicit)
functions.description: Initialize a DOCUMENT-START event with optional %YAML version directive, a list of %TAG directives, and an implicit flag. The implicit flag is stylistic and may be ignored by the emitter.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
version_directive may be NULL to omit the %YAML directive.
tag_directives_start and tag_directives_end define a half-open range [start, end) for %TAG directives; they may be NULL if there are no directives.
implicit is an int flag indicating whether the document start indicator is implicit.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_document_end_event_initialize
functions.description: Initialize a DOCUMENT-END event with an implicit flag. The implicit flag is stylistic and may be ignored by the emitter.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
implicit is an int flag indicating whether the document end indicator is implicit.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_alias_event_initialize
functions.description: Initialize an ALIAS event referencing a previously defined anchor name.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
anchor must be a valid NUL-terminated yaml_char_t string naming an existing anchor in the stream; must not be NULL as per parameter description.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_scalar_event_initialize
functions.signature: int yaml_scalar_event_initialize(yaml_event_t *event, const yaml_char_t *anchor, const yaml_char_t *tag, const yaml_char_t *value, int length, int plain_implicit, int quoted_implicit, yaml_scalar_style_t style)
functions.description: Initialize a SCALAR event with optional anchor and tag, scalar content and length, implicit flags, and a scalar style. The style may be ignored by the emitter. Either a tag must be provided or at least one of the implicit flags must be set.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
anchor may be NULL to omit an anchor.
tag may be NULL; if tag is NULL then at least one of plain_implicit or quoted_implicit must be non-zero.
value must be a valid pointer to the scalar bytes; length is the number of bytes of value.
plain_implicit and/or quoted_implicit must be set so that either tag is provided or an implicit flag is true (library requirement).
style must be a valid yaml_scalar_style_t.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_sequence_start_event_initialize
functions.signature: int yaml_sequence_start_event_initialize(yaml_event_t *event, const yaml_char_t *anchor, const yaml_char_t *tag, int implicit, yaml_sequence_style_t style)
functions.description: Initialize a SEQUENCE-START event with optional anchor and tag, an implicit flag, and a sequence style. The style may be ignored by the emitter. Either a tag must be provided or implicit must be set.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
anchor may be NULL to omit an anchor.
tag may be NULL; if tag is NULL then implicit must be non-zero.
implicit indicates that the tag may be omitted (must be set if tag is NULL).
style must be a valid yaml_sequence_style_t.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_sequence_end_event_initialize
functions.description: Initialize a SEQUENCE-END event, closing the most recent sequence started.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize
functions.signature: int yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize(yaml_event_t *event, const yaml_char_t *anchor, const yaml_char_t *tag, int implicit, yaml_mapping_style_t style)
functions.description: Initialize a MAPPING-START event with optional anchor and tag, an implicit flag, and a mapping style. The style may be ignored by the emitter. Either a tag must be provided or implicit must be set.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
anchor may be NULL to omit an anchor.
tag may be NULL; if tag is NULL then implicit must be non-zero.
implicit indicates that the tag may be omitted (must be set if tag is NULL).
style must be a valid yaml_mapping_style_t.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize
functions.description: Initialize a MAPPING-END event, closing the most recent mapping started.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_event_t.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_event_delete
functions.description: Free any memory owned by an event object previously produced or initialized. Leaves the event object in an undefined/empty state.
requirements: event must be a valid pointer to a yaml_event_t previously initialized/produced.
Do not use the event’s internal pointers after deletion.
Do not call yaml_event_delete twice on the same event object without reinitialization.

functions.name: yaml_document_initialize
functions.signature: int yaml_document_initialize(yaml_document_t *document, yaml_version_directive_t *version_directive, yaml_tag_directive_t *tag_directives_start, yaml_tag_directive_t *tag_directives_end, int start_implicit, int end_implicit)
functions.description: Create and initialize a YAML document with optional %YAML version and a list of %TAG directives, and with start/end implicit flags. Allocates internal structures to hold nodes.
requirements: document must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_document_t.
version_directive may be NULL to omit the %YAML directive.
tag_directives_start and tag_directives_end define a half-open range [start, end) of tag directives; they may be NULL if there are no directives.
start_implicit and end_implicit specify stylistic indicators.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_document_delete
functions.description: Delete a YAML document and all of its nodes, freeing associated memory.
requirements: document must be a valid pointer to a yaml_document_t previously initialized/loaded.
All node pointers obtained from this document become invalid after this call.
Do not call yaml_document_delete twice on the same document without reinitialization.

functions.name: yaml_document_get_node
functions.description: Return a pointer to the node with the given node id (index) within the document, or NULL if the index is out of range. The returned pointer remains valid until the document is modified or deleted.
requirements: document must be a valid pointer to an initialized yaml_document_t.
index should be a valid node id within the document; if out of range, the function returns NULL.
Do not use the returned node pointer after modifying or deleting the document.

functions.name: yaml_document_get_root_node
functions.description: Return a pointer to the root node of the document (the first node added), or NULL if the document is empty (which also signifies end of stream for parser-produced documents). The pointer remains valid until the document is modified or deleted.
requirements: document must be a valid pointer to an initialized yaml_document_t.
Do not use the returned node pointer after modifying or deleting the document.

functions.name: yaml_document_add_scalar
functions.signature: int yaml_document_add_scalar(yaml_document_t *document, const yaml_char_t *tag, const yaml_char_t *value, int length, yaml_scalar_style_t style)
functions.description: Create a SCALAR node with the given tag, value, and style, attach it to the document, and return the new node id. The style may be ignored by the emitter.
requirements: document must be a valid, initialized yaml_document_t pointer.
tag must be a valid, non-NULL tag string.
value must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the scalar bytes.
length must specify the length in bytes of value (exact semantics beyond this are not documented here).
Returns a positive node id on success or 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_document_add_sequence
functions.description: Create a SEQUENCE node with the given tag and style, attach it to the document, and return the new node id. The style may be ignored by the emitter.
requirements: document must be a valid, initialized yaml_document_t pointer.
tag must be a valid, non-NULL tag string.
style must be a valid yaml_sequence_style_t.
Returns a positive node id on success or 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_document_add_mapping
functions.signature: int yaml_document_add_mapping(yaml_document_t *document, const yaml_char_t *tag, yaml_mapping_style_t style)
functions.description: Create a MAPPING node with the given tag and style, attach it to the document, and return the new node id. The style may be ignored by the emitter.
requirements: document must be a valid, initialized yaml_document_t pointer.
tag must be a valid, non-NULL tag string.
style must be a valid yaml_mapping_style_t.
Returns a positive node id on success or 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_document_append_sequence_item
functions.description: Append an item node to an existing SEQUENCE node within the document.
requirements: document must be a valid, initialized yaml_document_t pointer.
sequence must be the node id of an existing SEQUENCE node in the same document.
item must be the node id of an existing node in the same document.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_document_append_mapping_pair
functions.signature: int yaml_document_append_mapping_pair(yaml_document_t *document, int mapping, int key, int value)
functions.description: Append a key/value pair to an existing MAPPING node within the document.
requirements: document must be a valid, initialized yaml_document_t pointer.
mapping must be the node id of an existing MAPPING node in the same document.
key and value must be node ids of existing nodes in the same document.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_parser_initialize
functions.description: Initialize a parser object for subsequent configuration and parsing. Caller must destroy it with yaml_parser_delete.
requirements: parser must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_parser_t.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value before use.
After initialization, the caller must set an input source via yaml_parser_set_input_string, yaml_parser_set_input_file, or yaml_parser_set_input before scanning/parsing/loading.

functions.name: yaml_parser_delete
functions.description: Destroy a parser object and free its internal resources.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer to a yaml_parser_t previously initialized by yaml_parser_initialize.
Do not use the parser after deletion.
Ensure no further scan/parse/load calls are made after deletion.

functions.name: yaml_parser_set_input_string
functions.signature: void yaml_parser_set_input_string(yaml_parser_t *parser, const unsigned char *input, size_t size)
functions.description: Configure the parser to read from a memory buffer. The input pointer must remain valid for the lifetime of the parser.
requirements: parser must be initialized by yaml_parser_initialize.
input must be a valid pointer to size bytes of data; it must remain valid while the parser object exists.
size is the number of bytes available at input.
The application is responsible for destroying/freeing input only after destroying the parser.

functions.name: yaml_parser_set_input_file
functions.description: Configure the parser to read from a FILE*. The file must be open for reading and will be read by the parser.
requirements: parser must be initialized by yaml_parser_initialize.
file must be a valid FILE* open for reading.
The application is responsible for closing the file.

functions.name: yaml_parser_set_input
functions.description: Configure the parser to read using a user-provided read handler callback and opaque data pointer.
requirements: parser must be initialized by yaml_parser_initialize.
handler must be a valid function pointer implementing yaml_read_handler_t semantics (return 1 on success, 0 on failure; set size_read to 0 on EOF).
data is passed back to the handler; its lifetime and thread-safety are the caller’s responsibility.

functions.name: yaml_parser_set_encoding
functions.description: Set the expected source encoding for the input stream.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
encoding must be a valid yaml_encoding_t value.

functions.name: yaml_parser_scan
functions.description: Scan the input and produce the next lexical token. Call repeatedly to iterate tokens from STREAM_START to STREAM_END. The caller must delete each produced token with yaml_token_delete.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured with an input source.
token must be a valid pointer to an empty yaml_token_t to be filled.
Do not alternate calls to yaml_parser_scan with yaml_parser_parse or yaml_parser_load; doing so will break the parser (library requirement).
Caller must call yaml_token_delete on any produced token to free associated buffers.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_parser_parse
functions.description: Parse the input and produce the next parsing event. Call repeatedly to iterate events from STREAM_START to STREAM_END. The caller must delete each produced event with yaml_event_delete.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured with an input source.
event must be a valid pointer to an empty yaml_event_t to be filled.
Do not alternate calls to yaml_parser_parse with yaml_parser_scan or yaml_parser_load; doing so will break the parser (library requirement).
Caller must call yaml_event_delete on any produced event to free associated buffers.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_parser_load
functions.description: Parse the input and produce the next complete YAML document. Call repeatedly to iterate documents in a stream. If the produced document has no root node, the end of the stream has been reached. The caller must delete each produced document with yaml_document_delete.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured with an input source.
document must be a valid pointer to an empty yaml_document_t to be filled.
Do not alternate calls to yaml_parser_load with yaml_parser_scan or yaml_parser_parse; doing so will break the parser (library requirement).
Caller must call yaml_document_delete on any produced document to free associated data.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_set_max_nest_level
functions.description: Set the maximum allowed depth of nested structures the parser will process. Default is 1000.
requirements: max is the maximum number of allowed nested events; exact valid range is not documented here.
Call this before parsing to affect subsequent parser behavior.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_initialize
functions.description: Initialize an emitter object for subsequent configuration and emission. Caller must destroy it with yaml_emitter_delete.
requirements: emitter must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an empty yaml_emitter_t.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value before use.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_delete
functions.description: Destroy an emitter object and free its internal resources.
requirements: emitter must be a valid pointer to a yaml_emitter_t previously initialized by yaml_emitter_initialize.
Do not use the emitter after deletion.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_output_string
functions.signature: void yaml_emitter_set_output_string(yaml_emitter_t *emitter, unsigned char *output, size_t size, size_t *size_written)
functions.description: Configure the emitter to write output bytes into a caller-provided buffer, reporting the number of bytes written. If the buffer is too small, the emitter signals YAML_WRITE_ERROR.
requirements: emitter must be initialized by yaml_emitter_initialize.
output must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes that remains valid for the emission period.
size specifies the buffer capacity in bytes.
size_written must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the number of bytes written.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_output_file
functions.description: Configure the emitter to write to a FILE*. The file must be open for writing; closing the file is the caller’s responsibility.
requirements: emitter must be initialized by yaml_emitter_initialize.
file must be a valid FILE* open for writing.
The application is responsible for closing the file.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_output
functions.description: Configure the emitter to write using a user-provided write handler callback and opaque data pointer.
requirements: emitter must be initialized by yaml_emitter_initialize.
handler must be a valid function pointer implementing yaml_write_handler_t semantics (return 1 on success, 0 on failure).
data is passed back to the handler; its lifetime and thread-safety are the caller’s responsibility.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_encoding
functions.description: Set the output encoding for the emitted stream.
requirements: emitter must be initialized.
encoding must be a valid yaml_encoding_t value.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_canonical
functions.description: Enable or disable canonical output formatting as defined by the YAML specification.
requirements: emitter must be initialized.
canonical is treated as a boolean flag (0/1).

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_indent
functions.description: Set the indentation increment for emitted YAML.
requirements: emitter must be initialized.
indent must satisfy 1 < indent < 10 (i.e., 2..9).

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_width
functions.description: Set the preferred maximum line width for emitted YAML; -1 means unlimited.
requirements: emitter must be initialized.
width must be -1 for unlimited or an application-chosen integer for preferred width (exact valid positive range not specified).

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_unicode
functions.description: Control whether unescaped non-ASCII (Unicode) characters are allowed in the output.
requirements: emitter must be initialized.
unicode is treated as a boolean flag (0/1).

functions.name: yaml_emitter_set_break
functions.description: Set the preferred line break style for emitted YAML.
requirements: emitter must be initialized.
line_break must be a valid yaml_break_t value.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_emit
functions.description: Emit a single event to the output stream. The emitter takes ownership of the event contents and will destroy them after emission, even on failure.
requirements: emitter must be initialized and configured with an output destination.
event must be a valid pointer to an initialized yaml_event_t (for example, from yaml_parser_parse or an initialize_* function).
Do not reuse or access the event’s content after calling this function (the emitter destroys it).
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_open
functions.description: Start a YAML stream on the emitter. Should be called before yaml_emitter_dump.
requirements: emitter must be initialized and configured with an output destination.
Call this before emitting documents with yaml_emitter_dump.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_close
functions.description: Finish the YAML stream on the emitter. Should be called after yaml_emitter_dump.
requirements: emitter must be initialized and an open stream should be active (typically after yaml_emitter_open).
Call this after emitting documents with yaml_emitter_dump.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_dump
functions.description: Emit a whole YAML document. The emitter takes ownership of the document contents and destroys them after emission, even on failure.
requirements: emitter must be initialized and configured with an output destination.
document must be a valid pointer to an initialized yaml_document_t (for example, from yaml_parser_load or yaml_document_initialize).
Do not reuse the document or its nodes after this call (the emitter destroys the content).
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: yaml_emitter_flush
functions.description: Flush any buffered output bytes to the destination.
requirements: emitter must be initialized and configured with an output destination.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error; caller must check the return value.

data_types.description: A YAML %TAG directive handle string. Typically begins and ends with '!' (e.g., '!h!' or '!yaml!'). Must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string consisting of characters valid for YAML tag handles.
A URI or IRI prefix used in YAML %TAG directives that maps a handle to a base URI (e.g., 'tag:example.com,2020:'). Must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string; typically conforms to URI syntax.
A full YAML tag (usually a URI-like string) used to identify the type of a node, e.g., 'tag:yaml.org,2002:str', 'tag:yaml.org,2002:seq', or a local tag like '!str'. NUL-terminated UTF-8.
Arbitrary byte sequence treated as scalar value content. May contain any bytes including NUL; in these stubs it is sourced from FUZZ_PARAM_STR and used with an explicit length.
A byte buffer containing YAML document text to be parsed. UTF-8 by default; may include any YAML content such as scalars, sequences, mappings, directives, and stream markers.
File contents read by the parser when configured with yaml_parser_set_input_file. The file data should contain YAML text; any bytes are possible for fuzzing.

A general-purpose NUL-terminated string used for identifiers like anchors or simple names. In this context used for YAML anchors or simple placeholders; may include non-alphanumeric characters in fuzzing but is treated as a generic C-string.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for YAML %TAG directive handle strings (UTF-8 bytes)
# Target stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to populate yaml_tag_directive_t.handle and .prefix
# Our buffers should therefore contain plausible YAML snippets that include %TAG directives
# with valid handles and prefixes to exercise different paths (0..2 directives, optional version, flags).
#
# We will generate a small YAML document preamble that may include:
# - Optional %YAML directive (versions 1.1 or 1.2)
# - 0, 1, or 2 %TAG directives with valid handles ('!h!' style) and diverse prefixes
# - A simple document start and minimal content to keep the parser/emitter happy when used as input
#
# The fuzzing harness obtains strings from FUZZ_PARAM_STR. Supplying a single buffer that contains
# multiple newline-separated candidates allows the harness (depending on integration) to slice or pull
# substrings; but to maximize compatibility, we structure the buffer as a YAML stream with directives
# and content so any extraction still yields valid handle/prefix substrings.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Valid characters for YAML tag handles (simplified practical subset): letters, digits, '-', '_'
_HANDLE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"

# Some interesting tag prefix URIs per YAML tag directive requirements
_BASE_PREFIXES = [
    b"tag:example.com,2020:",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:",
    b"!",  # local non-specific
    b"!!", # primary (non-specific) shorthand base
    b"tag:example.org,2001:test:",
    b"tag:foo.bar,1999:baz:",
]

def _rand_handle(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Typical handle: !<name>! where name uses allowed chars and non-empty
    length = rng.randint(1, 8)
    name = ''.join(rng.choice(_HANDLE_CHARS) for _ in range(length))
    return ("!" + name + "!").encode('utf-8')

def _rand_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(_BASE_PREFIXES)
    # Construct a custom, valid tag:domain,year:path: style
    domain_labels = [
        ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)))
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 3))
    ]
    domain = '.'.join(domain_labels)
    year = str(rng.randint(1990, 2030))
    path_parts = [
        ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + '-_') for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2))
    ]
    path = '' if not path_parts else ':'.join(path_parts) + ':'
    return f"tag:{domain},{year}:{path}".encode('utf-8')

def _yaml_version_line(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Libyaml fuzzer constrains version to major 1..2, minor 0..2
    major = rng.choice([1, 2])
    minor = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])
    return f"%YAML {major}.{minor}\n".encode('utf-8')

def _tag_directives_block(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> List[bytes]:
    lines = []
    # ensure unique handles if multiple
    seen = set()
    for _ in range(n):
        # generate unique handle
        for _retry in range(5):
            h = _rand_handle(rng)
            if h not in seen:
                seen.add(h)
                break
        p = _rand_prefix(rng)
        lines.append(b"%TAG " + h + b" " + p + b"\n")
    return lines

def _content_body(rng: random.Random, handles: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Produce a small mapping using optional explicit tags derived from the handles to ensure usage
    # Compose keys/values with simple scalars; sometimes use the handles in tags like !h!foo
    body_lines = []
    body_lines.append(b"---\n")
    use_flow = rng.random() < 0.3
    if use_flow:
        # simple flow mapping
        body_lines.append(b"{ a: 1, b: 2 }\n")
    else:
        body_lines.append(b"a: 1\n")
        body_lines.append(b"b: 2\n")
    # Optionally include a tagged scalar using one of our handles if present and prefix is set
    if handles and rng.random() < 0.8:
        tag_handle = rng.choice(handles)
        # Example: !h!foo as a key or value
        val = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8))).encode('utf-8')
        body_lines.append(tag_handle + val + b": tagged\n" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b"key: " + tag_handle + val + b"\n")
    body_lines.append(b"...\n")
    return b"".join(body_lines)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Optional %YAML line
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        chunks.append(_yaml_version_line(rng))

    # 0..2 %TAG directives
    n_tags = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])
    tag_lines = _tag_directives_block(rng, n_tags)
    chunks.extend(tag_lines)

    # Collect handles for later tagged scalars
    handles = []
    for tl in tag_lines:
        # tl is like b"%TAG !h! tag:...\n" -> extract handle between first space and second space
        try:
            parts = tl.strip().split()
            if len(parts) >= 3:
                handles.append(parts[1])
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Document start indicator is optional for emitter, include to keep input valid
    chunks.append(_content_body(rng, handles))

    out = b"".join(chunks)
    # Ensure limit and non-empty
    if not out:
        out = b"%TAG !h! tag:example.com,2020:\n---\nkey: val\n...\n"
    if len(out) > MAX_SIZE:
        out = out[:MAX_SIZE]
    return out

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator targets valid YAML %TAG directive inputs and related strings used by
# the provided fuzz stubs. It returns a single bytes buffer which, when consumed by
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM and similar in the harness, should yield interesting yet
# valid combinations of:
# - Optional %YAML version (1.0/1.1/2.0 variants per stub constraints)
# - 0..2 %TAG directives with valid handles and URI/IRI prefixes
# - Implicit flags
# The data model assumed by many harnesses is a linear byte stream consumed by the
# FUZZ_PARAM* primitives. We thus encode a compact, deterministic, valid sequence of
# parameters. The exact harness format is opaque, but providing a YAML document text
# exercising these features will feed both string and filename-based params usefully.
#
# Strategy: emit a single YAML stream text that embeds optional %YAML and several %TAG
# directives, then a small document that references tags and anchors so that downstream
# code paths are taken if used. The string is UTF-8 and <= 4096 bytes.

URI_PREFIX_SAMPLES = [
    b"tag:example.com,2020:",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:",
    b"https://schemas.example.org/yaml/",
    b"urn:example:yaml:",
    b"tag:ex.org,2019:types/",
]

# Valid YAML tag handles must start with '!' and end with '!' if named, or be '!' or '!!'.
HANDLE_SAMPLES = [
    b"!h!",
    b"!ex!",
    b"!t!",
    b"!!",        # primary handle
    b"!custom!",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "ümlaut", "日本語", "emoji-🙂", "δeta", "¡hola!", "данные",
]

SCALAR_SAMPLES = [
    b"hello",
    b"42",
    b"true",
    b"2025-12-14",
    b"line1\nline2",
]

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random) -> bool:
    return bool(r.getrandbits(1))

def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, arr):
    return arr[r.randrange(len(arr))]

def _rand_handle(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Occasionally emit bare '!' or '!!', mostly named handles !name!
    choice = r.randrange(6)
    if choice == 0:
        return b"!"
    if choice == 1:
        return b"!!"
    # Named: !<alnum>+!
    length = r.randrange(1, 6)
    name = bytes(''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters)), 'utf-8') if length == 1 else \
            bytes(''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(length)), 'utf-8')
    return b"!" + name + b"!"

def _rand_uri_prefix(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if _rand_bool(r):
        return _rand_choice(r, URI_PREFIX_SAMPLES)
    # Build a valid-ish tag: scheme:[host][,year]:[path]
    scheme = _rand_choice(r, [b"tag", b"http", b"https", b"urn"]) + b":"
    if scheme in (b"http:", b"https:"):
        host = b"//" + _rand_choice(r, [b"example.com", b"ex.org", b"yaml.org"]) + b"/"
        path_parts = [b"yaml", b"types", b"schemas", b"v1"]
        depth = r.randrange(0, 3)
        if depth:
            host += b"/".join(r.choice(path_parts) for _ in range(depth)) + (b"/" if _rand_bool(r) else b"")
        return scheme + host
    if scheme == b"tag:":
        host = _rand_choice(r, [b"example.com", b"ex.org", b"yaml.org"]) + b"," + \
               _rand_choice(r, [b"2002", b"2019", b"2020", b"2024"]) + b":"
        tail = b"types/" if _rand_bool(r) else b""
        return scheme + host + tail
    # urn
    return b"urn:" + _rand_choice(r, [b"example:yaml:", b"ex:types:", b"yaml:"])

def _rand_version(r: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Per stubs: major in {1,2}, minor in {0,1,2}
    return (1 + r.randrange(2), r.randrange(3))

def _yaml_header(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Optional %YAML version
    if _rand_bool(r):
        maj, minr = _rand_version(r)
        parts.append(f"%YAML {maj}.{minr}\n".encode('utf-8'))
    # 0..2 %TAG directives
    n = r.randrange(3)
    for _ in range(n):
        handle = _rand_handle(r)
        # Ensure empty in stubs replaced: here always non-empty
        if handle == b"":
            handle = b"!h!"
        prefix = _rand_uri_prefix(r)
        if prefix == b"":
            prefix = b"tag:example.com,2020:"
        parts.append(b"%TAG " + handle + b" " + prefix + b"\n")
    # Document start indicator, implicit vs explicit not expressed here; both valid
    parts.append(b"---\n")
    return b"".join(parts)

def _yaml_body(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a mapping with anchors, aliases, and optional tagged scalars
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    # Define an anchor
    key1 = b"key1"
    val1 = _rand_choice(r, SCALAR_SAMPLES)
    lines.append(b"&a1 " + val1 + b"\n")
    # Alias usage
    lines.append(b"alias: *a1\n")
    # A mapping
    lines.append(b"map:\n")
    # Optional custom tag using one of handles declared or primary (!!)
    tag_handle = _rand_choice(r, [b"!!", b"!ex!", b"!t!", b"!h!"])
    # YAML core tags include !!str/!!int etc.; use str or int randomly
    core_tag = _rand_choice(r, [b"str", b"int", b"bool"]) if tag_handle == b"!!" else b"scalar"
    value_utf8 = _rand_choice(r, SCALAR_SAMPLES)
    lines.append(b"  tagged: " + tag_handle + core_tag + b" " + value_utf8 + b"\n")
    # Add some unicode to exercise emitter unicode setting paths; YAML quoted scalar
    uni = r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    lines.append(("  unicode: \"" + uni + "\"\n").encode('utf-8'))
    # A small sequence
    lines.append(b"  list: [1, 2, 3]\n")
    return b"".join(lines)

def _yaml_footer(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Optionally explicit document end
    return b"...\n" if _rand_bool(r) else b""

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    header = _yaml_header(r)
    body = _yaml_body(r)
    footer = _yaml_footer(r)
    doc = header + body + footer
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(doc) > 4096:
        doc = doc[:4096]
    return doc

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid YAML tag URI strings (NUL-terminated UTF-8 when used as C strings
# by the fuzz stubs via std::string.c_str()). The fuzz target uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - YAML scalar/sequence/mapping event tags (may be NULL but often provided).
# - yaml_document_add_* tag parameters (must be non-NULL).
# Therefore, we generate a single bytes buffer that the harness will slice to populate multiple
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We pack multiple interesting tag strings separated by '\n'.
# The stubs already default to valid tags when empty, but providing rich, valid tags improves coverage.

CORE_TAGS = [
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:null",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:bool",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:int",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:float",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:str",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:seq",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:map",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:binary",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:timestamp",
]

# Some local and shorthand tags that are still syntactically valid as YAML tags.
LOCAL_TAGS = [
    b"!",
    b"!str",
    b"!seq",
    b"!map",
    b"!!str",
    b"!!seq",
    b"!!map",
    b"!custom",
    b"!my-app/type",
]

# A few URI-like and handle/prefix flavored tags to exercise parser acceptance.
MISC_TAGS = [
    b"tag:example.com,2025:widget",
    b"tag:example.org,2001:foo:bar",
    b"tag:example.net,1999:/ns/types/thing",
    b"!u!user/tag",
    b"!h!handle:part",
]

# Anchors and scalar values are also sourced from FUZZ_PARAM_STR in some stubs; include such lines too.
# They are not tags, but will still be valid UTF-8 strings; harness may use them for anchors/values.
ANCHORS = [b"a", b"A1", b"anchor_1", b"ref", b"x", b"root"]
SCALARS = [
    b"x",
    b"v",
    b"it",
    b"k",
    b"v2",
    "multiline line 1\nline 2".encode("utf-8"),
    "unicode  😀".encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"),
]

# Build additional random but valid tag URIs

def _random_core_or_local(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Either a core tag, local tag, or a syntactically valid tag:scheme
    choice = r.randint(0, 2)
    if choice == 0:
        return r.choice(CORE_TAGS)
    elif choice == 1:
        return r.choice(LOCAL_TAGS)
    else:
        # tag:domain,year:path[:more]
        dom_labels = [
            ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
            for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3))
        ]
        domain = '.'.join(dom_labels)
        year = str(r.randint(1990, 2035))
        # path segments
        segs = [
            ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + '-_') for _ in range(r.randint(2, 8)))
            for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3))
        ]
        path = '/'.join(segs)
        # optional extra colon section
        extra = ''
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            extra = ':' + ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)))
        s = f"tag:{domain},{year}:{path}{extra}"
        return s.encode('utf-8')


def _random_anchor(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return r.choice(ANCHORS)
    # random anchor: [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,7}
    start = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + '_')
    rest = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_-') for _ in range(r.randint(0, 7)))
    return (start + rest).encode('utf-8')


def _random_scalar(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> bytes:
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return r.choice(SCALARS)
    # Generate readable UTF-8 scalar with spaces and punctuation
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ' -_:/.,\t'
    n = r.randint(1, min(32, max_len))
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('utf-8')


def _assemble_lines(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    # Ensure presence of key canonical tags used by stubs
    lines.extend([b"tag:yaml.org,2002:str", b"tag:yaml.org,2002:seq", b"tag:yaml.org,2002:map"])  # for add_scalar/sequence/mapping

    # Add a mix of valid tags
    count_tags = r.randint(6, 14)
    for _ in range(count_tags):
        lines.append(_random_core_or_local(r))

    # Add anchors
    count_anchors = r.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(count_anchors):
        lines.append(_random_anchor(r))

    # Add scalar values used as content for value/key/value in document functions
    count_scalars = r.randint(5, 12)
    for _ in range(count_scalars):
        lines.append(_random_scalar(r))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order to keep buffer concise
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[bytes] = []
    for b in lines:
        if b not in seen:
            seen.add(b)
            uniq.append(b)
    return uniq


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    lines = _assemble_lines(r)
    # Join with newlines. FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls typically read slices from the buffer; providing
    # newline-separated entries makes it easy for the harness to split or pull substrings.
    buf = b"\n".join(lines)
    # Ensure buffer size <= 4096
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf

import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for valid, interesting YAML-related binary blobs used as scalar values and tags
# Target fuzzer stubs pull:
# - tag strings (default to standard tags if empty)
# - scalar values as arbitrary bytes with explicit length
# - style/enums chosen randomly by fuzzer
# Our job: provide a bytes buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR draws substrings from. We pack multiple
# interesting UTF-8 strings, valid YAML tags, anchors, URIs, Unicode scalars, and edge-case byte
# sequences (including NULs) into a single buffer, separated by varied delimiters so that random
# slicing still yields meaningful content.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

STD_TAGS = [
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:null",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:bool",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:int",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:float",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:str",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:seq",
    b"tag:yaml.org,2002:map",
]

# Additional custom tag prefixes/handles to encourage variety if stubs reuse as tags or values
EXTRA_TAGS = [
    b"!local!custom",
    b"!h!user",
    b"!env VAR",
    b"!<tag:example.com,2025:thing>",
]

# Interesting scalar values (valid UTF-8 plus edge cases)
SCALARS_TEXT = [
    b"",  # empty
    b"x",
    b"k",
    b"v",
    b"it",
    b"true",
    b"false",
    b"null",
    b"0",
    b"-1",
    b"3.14159",
    b"1e10",
    b".inf",
    b".nan",
    b"hello world",
    b"multi line\nsecond line\nthird line\n",
    b"key: value",
    b"- list\n- items\n- here\n",
    b"{a: 1, b: 2}",
    b"[1, 2, 3]",
    b"emoji: \xF0\x9F\x98\x80",  # 😀 UTF-8
    "こんにちは".encode("utf-8"),
    "mañana".encode("utf-8"),
    b"anchor_ref &a and *a",
    b"| literal style candidate\n  indented\n",
    b"> folded style candidate\n  indented\n",
]

# Binary edge cases including NULs and high bytes (still valid for libyaml scalar bytes)
SCALARS_BIN = [
    b"\x00",
    b"\x00\x00\x00",
    b"\x00END\x00",
    bytes(range(1, 32)),  # C0 control bytes (excluding NUL)
    bytes([0, 255, 254, 253, 1, 2, 3]),
    b"binary\x00with\x00nuls",
]

# Separators that are safe and varied; include NUL to allow embedded NUL cases
SEPS = [b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\0", b"\t", b"---\n", b"...\n", b"\x1f"]

# Build a pool of strings; FUZZ framework typically slices from a single blob

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _mix_sections(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    sections: list[bytes] = []

    # Ensure presence of standard tags to satisfy non-empty tag requirements in stubs
    tags = STD_TAGS + EXTRA_TAGS
    rng.shuffle(tags)
    sections.extend(tags)

    # Add scalar texts
    scalars = SCALARS_TEXT + SCALARS_BIN
    rng.shuffle(scalars)
    sections.extend(scalars)

    # Add varied keys/values likely to be used for mapping pairs
    kv_words = [b"alpha", b"beta", b"gamma", b"delta", b"key", b"value", b"name", b"id"]
    rng.shuffle(kv_words)
    sections.extend(kv_words[:rng.randint(4, len(kv_words))])

    # Include some URIs and prefixes that look like tag prefixes
    sections.extend([
        b"tag:example.org,2000:app/type",
        b"tag:foo,2020:bar/baz",
        b"!handle!prefix",
        b"!foo",
    ])

    # Anchors and aliases; even if parser side ignores here, they make good scalar content
    sections.extend([b"&anchor", b"*anchor", b"&a", b"*a"])

    # Include some random UTF-8 blobs and raw bytes to diversify
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        # Create a short random UTF-8 string
        s = ''.join(chr(rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E)) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)))
        sections.append(s.encode('utf-8'))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        sections.append(_rand_bytes(rng, 5, 20))

    return sections


def _interleave(sections: list[bytes], rng: random.Random, max_size: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Start with a document header sometimes to seed good tags when sliced
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        out += b"%YAML 1.2\n"
        out += b"%TAG ! tag:yaml.org,2002:\n"
        out += b"---\n"
    # Interleave sections with varied separators to allow FUZZ_PARAM_STR to pick useful spans
    for i, s in enumerate(sections):
        if len(out) + len(s) > max_size:
            break
        out += s
        if i + 1 < len(sections):
            sep = rng.choice(SEPS)
            if len(out) + len(sep) > max_size:
                break
            out += sep
    # Ensure we do not exceed limit
    return bytes(out[:max_size])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    sections = _mix_sections(rng)
    blob = _interleave(sections, rng, MAX_SIZE)

    # If blob ended up empty (shouldn't), fall back to a default valid tag and simple value
    if not blob:
        blob = b"tag:yaml.org,2002:str\nhello\n"

    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets YAML event-initializer stubs that request strings for:
# - anchors (must be non-empty C-strings)
# - tags and handles/prefixes in %TAG directives
# - scalar values
# It also benefits from occasionally providing multiple NUL-terminated strings
# in one buffer so FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can draw distinct substrings.
# We therefore build a buffer consisting of several NUL-terminated strings with
# a mix of YAML-relevant tokens and random content, plus some ASCII/UTF-8.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits

# Some interesting YAML-related lexical pieces
YAML_ANCHORS = [
    "a", "id", "anchor", "A1", "x", "root", "seq", "map", "k", "v",
]
YAML_TAGS = [
    "!", "!!str", "!!map", "!!seq", "!str", "!map", "!seq",
    "tag:yaml.org,2002:str", "tag:yaml.org,2002:int", "tag:example.com,2025:custom",
]
YAML_HANDLES = [
    "!", "!!", "!foo!", "!bar!",
]
YAML_PREFIXES = [
    "tag:yaml.org,2002:", "tag:example.com,2025:", "!local:", "urn:example:y:"
]
SCALAR_SAMPLES = [
    "v", "value", "hello", "true", "false", "null", "0", "12345",
    "line one\nline two", "with spaces", "quoted\"value", "single'quote",
    "unicode: café ☕", "dash-start", "#hash", ":colon", "[brackets]", "{brace}",
]

# Helper to make a safe C-string segment (no embedded NULs)
def _rand_c_string(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix of alnum and selected punctuation to exercise tags/handles
    charset = ALNUM + "-_:/.,#[]{}()!$%&+@"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(charset) for _ in range(length))

# Build a list of NUL-terminated strings targeted to the stub calls
# Order matters because the fuzz harness will likely consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# multiple times per invocation. We provide a rich set to cover branches.

def _build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Potential %TAG directive pairs (handle, prefix) repeated
    n_tag_pairs = rng.randint(0, 2)
    for _ in range(n_tag_pairs):
        handle = rng.choice(YAML_HANDLES + [ _rand_c_string(rng, 1, 6) + "!" ])
        prefix = rng.choice(YAML_PREFIXES + ["tag:example.org,2000:" + _rand_c_string(rng,1,6)])
        out.append(handle.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")
        out.append(prefix.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 2) Anchors for alias/sequence/mapping/scalar (must be non-empty)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        anchor = rng.choice(YAML_ANCHORS + [ _rand_c_string(rng,1,8) ])
        out.append(anchor.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 3) Possible tags
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        tag = rng.choice(YAML_TAGS + ["!" + _rand_c_string(rng,1,6)])
        out.append(tag.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 4) Scalar values of varying sizes and characters
    samples = SCALAR_SAMPLES[:]
    # Add some random ones
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        samples.append(_rand_c_string(rng, 1, rng.randint(4, 32)))
    # Shuffle and pick a subset
    rng.shuffle(samples)
    for s in samples[:rng.randint(4, 10)]:
        out.append(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 5) Extra random strings to satisfy any additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        out.append(_rand_c_string(rng, 1, 24).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    return out

# We also include some unsigned ints for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) draws by
# embedding them as ASCII decimal strings the harness may not use; however,
# FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) isn’t from our buffer. The important part is strings.


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Compose multiple NUL-terminated strings in sequence.
    parts = _build_strings(rng)

    # Ensure total size cap
    data = b"".join(parts)
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Ensure buffer ends with NUL to not cut a string mid-way
        if not data.endswith(b"\x00"):
            # Trim back to last NUL if present, else append one if room
            last_nul = data.rfind(b"\x00")
            if last_nul != -1:
                data = data[:last_nul+1]
            else:
                data = data[:-1] + b"\x00"

    # Always ensure non-empty and at least one NUL-terminated minimal string
    if not data:
        data = b"a\x00"

    return data
